## Proposed change
Reimplement the mycroft notification component using mycroft-messagebus-client
This resolves the issue with the mycroftapi==2.0 depending on an ancient websocket-client, which was the reason for disabling the component in the first place

Removes requirement for "mycroftapi==2.0" (in the manifest)
Adds requirement for "mycroft-messagebus-client==0.10.1" (in manifest and requirements_all.txt)

issue_context.title: Mycroft integration disabled due to dependency problem
issue_context.body:
### The problem

he notification component for mycroft has been [disabled since Apr 27, 2023](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/cdbffee7814380b10952f9ac7f8a1e6bc6e93861)
The component was depending on a really old abandoned project that was causing problems. See: [thread on mycroftapi==2.0 issue](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/10788#issuecomment-1012591304)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.7.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2023.5

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Container

### Integration causing the issue

Mycroft

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mycroft

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

I have reimplemented the component using MessageBusClient from [mycroft-messagebus-client>=0.9.4](https://github.com/MycroftAI/mycroft-messagebus-client) instead and allows for relaxing the requirements for the websocket-client version.

mycroft-messagebus-client>=0.9.4 depends on websocket-client>=0.54.0 and pyee==8.1.0 which is almost four years old now.
comments: Okay, so what's the point of this issue? If you want to implement it, feel free to open a PR
The point is to refer to it in the PR I'm opening right now :D
Gotta do some more checking, but I'll open the PR tomorrow.
You don't have to open an issue to do a PR, just explain what you want to do in the PR itself and that's fine
OK PR out now. This is my first PR in this fine project so I was wondering whether I should keep rebasing my branch when it's out of date?

You probably don't have to do that very much. Since integrations are in different folders, other changes don't affect yours much. Unless there are core changes, in which case it's good to maybe rebase once per month or so.

But I'll close this issue since there is no real point of keeping this open

review_comments: Please create the bus and start the thread in `get_service`. Then just pass the bus instance to `MycroftNotificationService`.

We need to clean up the thread when Home Assistant stops. We can listen for the Home Assistant stop event and register an event handler that closes the websocket.

Alternatively, since we don't actually need to listen for incoming websocket messages, maybe just use this helper function that doesn't keep the websocket open?

https://github.com/MycroftAI/mycroft-messagebus-client/blob/01ade972facb9c2287d4b9eade49b7f8c1e74655/mycroft_bus_client/send_func.py#L30

Thank you for your educational feedback. As that package still depends on the pinned pyee and the development of mycroft has stopped, I decided to fork the mycroft-messagebus-client and resolve the issue myself. Having the websocket open on load gives an early warning about potential issues before it's time to deliver the message, so I'd prefer using the websocket as intended. Plus I'd get some experience publishing on PyPi. Implementing this using plain websocket-client would be fairly simple, but that would then lead to having to pin websocket-client and I'm pretty sure that could lead to much collateral damage and enemies I don't want to make.

Ok. Please pick a name that is distinctly different from mycroft-messagebus-client and ask GitHub to disconnect your fork from upstream once you've published a new version.

Forks that are meant to have separate development than their upstream should not be connected to upstream anymore.
